matches.rationale: GT1 concerns inflated dataset size claims in the abstract (48,000 vs actual ~24,000 pairs). Finding 1 addresses a misattributed depth estimation citation in the degradation model section. These are entirely different scientific issues in different locations.

GT2 identifies swapped query matrices in cross-attention (Section 4.3.1) as a method logic error. No finding addresses cross-attention query/key/value inconsistencies or transformer fusion mechanisms.

GT3 concerns asymmetric experimental protocol in Table 2 where the proposed method uses preprocessing restoration methods while baselines do not. No finding discusses experimental design asymmetry or preprocessing advantages.
GT4 identifies overclaimed robustness in the introduction without acknowledging limitations. No finding addresses exaggerated claims about handling degradations or user flexibility.

GT5 concerns fabricated reference [8] (AutoDIR) in Related Work. Finding 1 addresses reference [40] misattribution for depth estimation. These are different references with different fabrication/misattribution issues.
GT6 identifies missing ethical considerations in the conclusion. No finding addresses ethical omissions, bias, or transparency concerns.
GT7 concerns promotional exaggeration in the abstract without acknowledging limitations. No finding addresses rhetorical tone or overstated performance claims.
GT8 identifies inconsistency between claimed GitHub code availability in abstract and lack of details elsewhere. No finding addresses code availability or reproducibility documentation issues.
GT9 concerns unclear loss function application (symmetric vs. asymmetric) in Stage II training. No finding addresses loss function design or multi-objective optimization inconsistencies.
GT10 identifies potentially problematic small batch size (12) and patch size (224×224) without discussion. No finding addresses training configuration or batch size concerns.
GT11 concerns selective interpretation of mixed results where some metrics are not best but claimed as dominant. No finding addresses cherry-picked metric reporting or overstated superiority claims.
GT12 identifies overly optimistic framing of degradation model transferability in discussion. No finding addresses limitations in model generalization or transferability claims.

GT13 concerns fabricated 2025 references [38] and [43] beyond knowledge cutoff. Finding 1 addresses reference [40] misattribution but for a different reference and different issue (wrong method vs. impossible date).
GT14 identifies missing ethical considerations about dataset privacy and safety-critical applications in experiments section. No finding addresses ethical omissions or responsible AI concerns.

GT15 identifies inconsistency between text claim (best on CLIP-IQA, TReS, SD) and Table 3 showing Text-DiFuse better on MUSIQ. No finding addresses this table-text inconsistency or selective result interpretation.
